ACCOUNT CONTROL AGREEMENT
TRACKED-CHANGES REDLINE
(Counterparty Draft → Lender/Secured Party Position)

Document: Account Control Agreement (Deposit Account)
Parties: [Borrower / Debtor]; [Depository Bank]; [Administrative Agent / Secured Party]
Facility: Senior Secured Credit Agreement (Executed)
Base Sources Reconciled: Internal ACA Playbook; Executed Credit Agreement; Depository Bank Standard Form; Account Schedule & Related Correspondence/Checklists; Counterparty Markup
Status: COUNSEL REDLINE — FOR NEGOTIATION
Legend: [DELETE: text proposed for deletion]  [INSERT: text proposed for insertion]  [MOVE/RESTRUCTURE notes in braces]

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
PREAMBLE / RECITALS
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

This ACCOUNT CONTROL AGREEMENT (this “Agreement”) is entered into as of [Effective Date], by and among:

(i) [BORROWER LEGAL NAME], a [jurisdiction] [entity type] (the “Debtor”);
(ii) [DEPOSITORY BANK LEGAL NAME] (the “Bank”); and
(iii) [ADMINISTRATIVE AGENT NAME], as administrative agent and collateral agent for the Secured Parties under the Credit Agreement (in such capacities, the “Secured Party”).

Recitals.
A. Debtor, the lenders party thereto, and Secured Party have entered into that certain Credit Agreement dated as of [CA Date] (as amended, restated, supplemented or otherwise modified from time to time, the “Credit Agreement”).
B. Debtor has granted to Secured Party a security interest in, among other things, the Deposit Account (as defined below) pursuant to the Security Agreement and the Credit Agreement.
C. The parties enter into this Agreement to perfect Secured Party’s control over the Deposit Account under Articles 8 and 9 of the Uniform Commercial Code as in effect in the State of New York (the “UCC”), and to set forth the Bank’s duties with respect to the Deposit Account.

[INSERT: D. Capitalized terms used but not defined herein have the meanings ascribed in the Credit Agreement. In the event of any conflict between this Agreement and the Credit Agreement with respect to the rights of the Secured Party against the Debtor, the Credit Agreement shall control as between Secured Party and Debtor; provided that nothing in the Credit Agreement shall impair the Bank’s rights, protections, or exculpations expressly set forth herein.]

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
ARTICLE I — DEFINITIONS
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Section 1.1 Defined Terms.

“Account Details” means the deposit account(s) identified on Schedule A (Account Schedule), including account number, account title, ABA/routing number, and account type, as updated from time to time by written notice from Secured Party and Debtor to Bank in accordance with Section 8.3.

“Control” has the meaning set forth in Sections 8-106 and 9-104 of the UCC.

“Credit Agreement” has the meaning set forth in the Recitals.

[DELETE: “Indemnification Cap” means an aggregate amount equal to twelve (12) months of fees paid to the Bank under this Agreement.]
[INSERT: “Indemnification Cap” means, with respect to the Bank’s indemnification obligations solely for ordinary negligence (and expressly excluding the Excluded Matters), an aggregate amount equal to the greater of (x) all fees paid to the Bank under this Agreement during the thirty-six (36) month period immediately preceding the claim and (y) $5,000,000; provided that the Indemnification Cap shall not apply to any Excluded Matter.]

[INSERT: “Excluded Matter” means any Loss arising out of or relating to (i) the Bank’s gross negligence, willful misconduct, or bad faith, (ii) the Bank’s breach of the exclusive control, entitlement-order, or freeze obligations under Article III, (iii) the Bank’s failure to comply with a Notice of Exclusive Control or entitlement order after the Effectiveness Time, (iv) fraud or criminal conduct of the Bank or its officers, employees, or agents, or (v) any claim with respect to which indemnification may not be limited as a matter of applicable law.]

[DELETE: “Material Adverse Effect” means a material adverse effect on (a) the business, assets, properties, liabilities, or financial condition of the Debtor and its subsidiaries, taken as a whole; provided that none of the following shall constitute or be taken into account in determining whether a Material Adverse Effect has occurred or would reasonably be expected to occur: (i) changes in general economic or political conditions; (ii) changes in GAAP or applicable law; (iii) acts of war or terrorism; (iv) any regulatory action, investigation, enforcement proceeding, consent order, fine, sanction, or supervisory directive by any Governmental Authority (including bank regulatory, consumer financial, anti-money-laundering, sanctions, or prudential regulators) affecting the Debtor, the Deposit Account, the Bank, or the transactions contemplated hereby; or (v) the announcement or pendency of this Agreement or the Credit Agreement.]
[INSERT: “Material Adverse Effect” means a material adverse effect on (a) the business, assets, properties, liabilities (actual or contingent), or financial condition of the Debtor and its subsidiaries, taken as a whole, (b) the ability of the Debtor to perform its obligations under this Agreement, the Credit Agreement, or any other Loan Document, (c) the legality, validity, binding effect, or enforceability of this Agreement or any Lien granted to the Secured Party, or (d) the rights and remedies of the Secured Party under this Agreement or any Loan Document, or the validity, perfection, or priority of any Lien in favor of the Secured Party on the Deposit Account or other Collateral; provided that none of the following shall constitute or be taken into account in determining whether a Material Adverse Effect under clause (a) only has occurred or would reasonably be expected to occur (except, in each case, to the extent having a disproportionate adverse effect on the Debtor and its subsidiaries, taken as a whole, relative to other participants in the same industry): (i) changes in general economic, financial market, or political conditions; (ii) changes in GAAP or applicable law after the date hereof of general applicability; (iii) acts of war, terrorism, or natural disasters; and (iv) the announcement or pendency of the Credit Agreement or this Agreement. For the avoidance of doubt, no regulatory action, investigation, enforcement proceeding, consent order, fine, sanction, supervisory directive, or similar action by any Governmental Authority shall be carved out of Material Adverse Effect, and any such action may constitute or contribute to a Material Adverse Effect under any of clauses (a)–(d).]

[DELETE: “Survival Period” means, with respect to the representations and warranties in Article IV, a period of twelve (12) months following the termination of this Agreement.]
[INSERT: “Survival Period” means (a) with respect to the Fundamental Representations, a period ending on the date that is ninety (90) days after the expiration of the applicable statute of limitations (including any extensions or waivers), (b) with respect to the Bank’s representations regarding authority, enforceability, no conflict with bank regulatory requirements applicable to control agreements, and creation of Control, survival without temporal limitation (or, if a limitation is required by Bank policy, not less than six (6) years following termination of this Agreement), and (c) with respect to all other representations and warranties in Article IV, a period of thirty-six (36) months following the earlier of termination of this Agreement and the Discharge Date.]

[INSERT: “Fundamental Representations” means the representations and warranties set forth in Sections 4.1 (Organization; Power), 4.2 (Authorization; Enforceability), 4.3 (No Conflict), 4.4 (Deposit Account; Title; Control), 4.5 (No Prior Control Agreements; Priority), and 4.6 (Compliance with Laws; Sanctions; AML) (and any corresponding Bank or Debtor representations covering the same subject matter).]

[INSERT: “Notice of Exclusive Control” or “NOEC” means a written notice from Secured Party to Bank substantially in the form of Exhibit B (or such other form as Bank and Secured Party may reasonably agree), stating that Secured Party is exercising exclusive control over the Deposit Account.]

[INSERT: “Effectiveness Time” means the time Bank receives a Notice of Exclusive Control that complies with Section 3.2.]

[INSERT: “Discharge Date” means the date on which (i) all Obligations under the Credit Agreement have been indefeasibly paid in full in cash, (ii) all Letters of Credit have been cash-collateralized or backstopped on terms satisfactory to the applicable Issuing Bank, (iii) all Commitments have been terminated, and (iv) Secured Party has delivered a written termination notice to Bank releasing control.]

[INSERT: “Indemnified Person” means Secured Party, each Secured Party (as defined in the Credit Agreement), and each of their respective officers, directors, employees, agents, advisors, and controlling persons.]

[INSERT: “Losses” means any and all claims, damages, losses, liabilities, costs, and expenses (including reasonable and documented out-of-pocket fees and expenses of counsel), whether or not arising out of third-party claims.]

[DELETE: “Basket” means $250,000, which shall operate as a tipping basket such that once aggregate Losses exceed the Basket, the indemnifying party shall be liable for all Losses from the first dollar.]
[INSERT: “Basket” means $500,000, which shall operate solely as a deductible (true deductible). The indemnifying party shall be liable only for Losses in excess of the Basket, and only from and after the time aggregate indemnifiable Losses exceed the Basket; Losses below the Basket shall not be recoverable. The Basket shall not apply to Excluded Matters, Fundamental Representations, or fraud.]

Other terms. “Business Day,” “Governmental Authority,” “Lien,” “Loan Documents,” “Obligations,” and “Secured Parties” have the meanings assigned in the Credit Agreement unless otherwise defined herein.

Section 1.2 UCC Terms. Terms defined in the UCC and not otherwise defined herein have the UCC meanings. The term “deposit account” has the meaning in UCC § 9-102.

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
ARTICLE II — THE DEPOSIT ACCOUNT; ACKNOWLEDGMENT OF SECURITY INTEREST
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Section 2.1 Identification of Deposit Account.
Bank maintains for Debtor the deposit account(s) described on Schedule A (the “Deposit Account”). Debtor and Bank represent that Schedule A is complete and accurate as of the date hereof. [INSERT: Any additional or substitute account intended to constitute a “Deposit Account” under this Agreement shall be added only by a written supplement to Schedule A executed by Debtor, Bank, and Secured Party (email PDF acceptable if followed by original signatures if Bank so requires).]

Section 2.2 Security Interest; Subordination of Bank Liens.
Debtor has granted to Secured Party a security interest in the Deposit Account and all cash, checks, wire transfers, investment property, and other items from time to time credited thereto (collectively, the “Account Collateral”). Bank acknowledges the security interest. [INSERT: Bank subordinates any security interest, right of set-off, banker’s lien, counterclaim, or other right Bank may have in or against the Account Collateral to the security interest and Control of Secured Party, except for (a) Bank’s fees and charges for maintaining the Deposit Account expressly described on Schedule B and incurred in the ordinary course, and (b) returned items and reversals for items credited in error, in each case solely to the extent not resulting from Bank’s failure to comply with this Agreement; provided that after the Effectiveness Time, Bank shall not exercise any set-off, recoupment, or banker’s lien against the Deposit Account without Secured Party’s prior written consent, other than for returned items posted prior to the Effectiveness Time.]

[INSERT: Section 2.3 No Other Control Arrangements. Bank represents and agrees that it has not entered into, and will not enter into, any other control agreement, lockbox agreement, or similar arrangement with respect to the Deposit Account in favor of any person other than Secured Party, except with Secured Party’s prior written consent. Bank has not authenticated any control agreement currently in effect with respect to the Deposit Account other than this Agreement.]

[INSERT: Section 2.4 Account Type; Location. Bank confirms the Deposit Account is a “deposit account” as defined in UCC § 9-102, is maintained in the ordinary course of Bank’s deposit-taking business, and is located in [State], for purposes of UCC §§ 9-304 and 9-305. Bank is a “bank” as defined in UCC § 9-102.]

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
ARTICLE III — CONTROL; ENTITLEMENT ORDERS; EXCLUSIVE CONTROL
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Section 3.1 Control Agreement (UCC § 9-104(a)(2)).
Bank agrees to comply with instructions originated by Secured Party directing disposition of funds in the Deposit Account without further consent by Debtor. [INSERT: This Agreement is intended to confer “control” upon Secured Party within the meaning of UCC §§ 8-106 and 9-104. Bank will not require Debtor’s consent as a condition to complying with Secured Party’s instructions or entitlement orders.]

Section 3.2 Notice of Exclusive Control.
Until Bank receives a Notice of Exclusive Control from Secured Party:
(a) Bank may comply with instructions from Debtor concerning the Deposit Account (including withdrawals and transfers); and
(b) Secured Party agrees not to originate instructions except as permitted under the Credit Agreement (as between Secured Party and Debtor only; Bank may rely on any instruction from Secured Party without investigating compliance with the Credit Agreement).

[INSERT: Upon the Effectiveness Time:
(i) Bank shall immediately cease complying with instructions from Debtor with respect to the Deposit Account;
(ii) Bank shall comply solely with instructions and entitlement orders originated by Secured Party;
(iii) Bank shall not permit any withdrawal, transfer, payment, or other disposition of Account Collateral except as directed by Secured Party, other than posting of returned items as expressly permitted in Section 2.2; and
(iv) Bank shall, within one (1) Business Day, confirm in writing to Secured Party receipt of the NOEC and the balance of the Deposit Account as of the Effectiveness Time.]

[DELETE: Bank shall use commercially reasonable efforts to comply with a Notice of Exclusive Control within five (5) Business Days after receipt.]
[INSERT: Bank shall comply with a Notice of Exclusive Control and all entitlement orders from Secured Party as soon as reasonably practicable and in any event no later than the close of business on the Business Day of receipt if received before 12:00 noon (Bank local time), and otherwise by the close of business on the next Business Day. Time is of the essence with respect to Bank’s exclusive-control obligations.]

Section 3.3 Form of Instructions.
Instructions and the NOEC shall be in writing (including PDF by email to the notice addresses in Section 8.1) [INSERT: or by such secure electronic channel as Bank and Secured Party implement], and shall be sent by authorized persons identified on Exhibit C (as updated). [INSERT: Bank shall be entitled to rely on instructions that appear on their face to be from an authorized person of Secured Party, without duty of further inquiry, absent actual knowledge of lack of authority.]

[INSERT: Section 3.4 No Dual Control / Standing Instructions. Bank shall not honor any standing restriction requiring dual approval of Debtor and Secured Party after the Effectiveness Time. Any “springing” or “blocked” account mechanics shall operate strictly in accordance with this Article III and shall not condition Secured Party’s Control on Debtor’s countersignature.]

[INSERT: Section 3.5 Sweep / Zero-Balance / Related Accounts. If the Deposit Account is subject to any sweep, ZBA, concentration, or similar arrangement, Bank and Debtor shall ensure such arrangements are subordinated to Secured Party’s Control and terminate automatically at the Effectiveness Time unless Secured Party otherwise directs in writing. Related accounts used solely as conduits shall be listed on Schedule A or expressly excluded in writing satisfactory to Secured Party.]

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
ARTICLE IV — REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Section 4.1 Organization; Power.
Each of Debtor and Bank represents that it is duly organized, validly existing, and in good standing under the laws of its jurisdiction of organization and has full power and authority to enter into and perform this Agreement.

Section 4.2 Authorization; Enforceability.
This Agreement has been duly authorized, executed, and delivered and constitutes a legal, valid, and binding obligation, enforceable in accordance with its terms, subject to bankruptcy, insolvency, and general equitable principles.

Section 4.3 No Conflict.
Execution and performance do not conflict with organizational documents, material agreements, or applicable law [INSERT: in any manner that would materially impair Control, perfection, or priority of Secured Party’s interest in the Account Collateral].

Section 4.4 Deposit Account; Title; Control.
Debtor represents it is the sole account holder of the Deposit Account (except as noted on Schedule A) and has not granted any other person Control or a competing security interest in the Account Collateral except as permitted under the Credit Agreement and disclosed in writing to Secured Party. Bank represents that the Account Details are true and complete and that this Agreement is sufficient under Bank’s policies and applicable law to establish Secured Party’s Control.

[INSERT: Section 4.5 No Prior Control Agreements; Priority. Bank represents that (a) no other control agreement is in effect for the Deposit Account, (b) Bank has not received notice of any other adverse claim to the Deposit Account except as disclosed on Schedule A, and (c) upon establishment of Control hereunder, Secured Party’s security interest will be perfected by control with priority over any conflicting unperfected interest and over any interest perfected solely by filing, to the extent provided in the UCC.]

[INSERT: Section 4.6 Compliance with Laws; Sanctions; AML. Each party represents that it will comply with applicable sanctions, anti-money-laundering, and banking laws in connection with the Deposit Account. Debtor represents that none of the Account Collateral is derived from unlawful activity. Bank represents that maintenance of the Deposit Account and performance of this Agreement do not violate any regulatory order binding on Bank of which Bank has knowledge.]

[DELETE: All representations and warranties shall survive for the Survival Period of twelve (12) months after termination only, and thereafter shall terminate in full, including as to then-pending claims.]
[INSERT: Section 4.7 Survival. All representations and warranties shall survive execution and delivery of this Agreement and shall continue for the applicable Survival Period. Claims asserted in writing in reasonable detail prior to the end of the applicable Survival Period shall survive until finally resolved. Fundamental Representations and claims based on fraud or willful misconduct shall survive as provided in the definition of Survival Period. No shortened limitation period in this Agreement shall shorten any statute of limitations applicable to fraud or to enforcement of Control or priority.]

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
ARTICLE V — COVENANTS
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Section 5.1 Debtor Covenants.
Debtor shall: (a) maintain the Deposit Account in good standing; (b) not permit any other control agreement or assignment of the Deposit Account without Secured Party’s prior written consent; (c) not change the account name, number, or bank without prior written notice to and consent of Secured Party and an updated control agreement or joinder; [INSERT: (d) direct all proceeds of Collateral required by the Credit Agreement to be deposited into the Deposit Account; (e) not close the Deposit Account without Secured Party’s prior written consent; and (f) provide Secured Party promptly upon request with account statements and transaction detail (to the extent Bank permits or Debtor can obtain).]

Section 5.2 Bank Covenants.
Bank shall: (a) maintain the Deposit Account as a deposit account; (b) not change its name or the location of the Deposit Account in a manner that adversely affects perfection without at least thirty (30) days’ prior written notice to Secured Party; [INSERT: (c) provide to Secured Party, upon request after the Effectiveness Time (and, if agreed, before), copies of account statements and balance information; (d) promptly notify Secured Party if Bank receives any notice of levy, garnishment, adverse claim, or other legal process regarding the Deposit Account; and (e) not amend account documentation in a manner that conflicts with this Agreement.]

[INSERT: Section 5.3 Credit Agreement Alignment. Debtor shall comply with all deposit account control, cash management, and blocked account requirements of the Credit Agreement. A Default or Event of Default under the Credit Agreement shall entitle Secured Party to deliver a NOEC hereunder without any additional cure period under this Agreement.]

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
ARTICLE VI — INDEMNIFICATION; LIMITATION OF LIABILITY; BASKET
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Section 6.1 Indemnification by Debtor.
Debtor shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Bank and each Indemnified Person from and against any and all Losses arising out of or relating to this Agreement or the Deposit Account, except to the extent resulting from the indemnified person’s gross negligence or willful misconduct [INSERT: as determined by a final non-appealable judgment of a court of competent jurisdiction].

Section 6.2 Indemnification by Bank / Limitations — REDLINED.
[DELETE: Bank’s aggregate liability under this Agreement shall not exceed the Indemnification Cap equal to twelve (12) months of fees paid to Bank. All indemnification claims against Bank are subject to a tipping basket of $250,000 (once exceeded, recovery from dollar one). Bank shall have no liability for consequential, special, indirect, or punitive damages. The foregoing limitations apply to all claims including those arising from Bank’s negligence, failure to comply with entitlement orders, or operational errors.]

[INSERT: (a) Subject to clause (b), Bank’s aggregate liability for Losses arising solely from ordinary negligence in the performance of ministerial duties under this Agreement shall not exceed the Indemnification Cap.
(b) The Indemnification Cap, the Basket, and any exclusion of consequential damages shall NOT apply to Excluded Matters. Without limiting the foregoing, Bank remains fully liable, without cap or basket, for Losses arising from Excluded Matters.

args.body:
ISSUES AND RISK MEMORANDUM
Account Control Agreement — Counterparty Paper Review
Confidential — Attorney Work Product

TO:        File / Deal Team / Partner
FROM:      Contracts Counsel
RE:        Review of Counterparty Draft Account Control Agreement — Deviations, Missing Protections, Off-Market Terms, and Recommended Positions
MATTER:    contracts work: Review Account Control Agreement Counterparty Paper
DATE:      [Engagement Date]
RELATED:   aca-redline.docx (tracked-changes redline implementing all recommended modifications)

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

We reviewed the counterparty’s draft Account Control Agreement (“ACA” or “Agreement”) against: (i) the firm’s internal ACA playbook; (ii) the executed senior secured Credit Agreement and related Security Agreement; (iii) the depository bank’s standard control-agreement form and customary market ACA terms; (iv) the account details / Schedule A materials; and (v) related correspondence and closing checklists.

The counterparty draft accepts a substantial portion of firm-standard architecture but introduces three material, adverse deviations that must be reversed, and omits several control-perfection and enforcement protections that are standard for secured-party / agent paper and required for alignment with the Credit Agreement:

  1. Silent reduction of the indemnification cap and conversion of the loss basket from a true deductible into a tipping basket (HIGH).
  2. Material Adverse Effect definition expanded with regulatory-action carve-outs that neutralize precisely the risk profile relevant to this facility and deposit-account enforcement (HIGH).
  3. Shortened survival / limitation period for core representations, including purported extinguishment after twelve months (HIGH).

In addition, the draft is missing or weak on: express UCC § 9-104 control language and exclusive-control timing; Bank lien subordination and post-NOEC set-off freeze; no-other-control-agreement / priority reps; sweep-ZBA termination at NOEC; termination mechanics that protect control through Discharge; Credit Agreement default alignment; order-of-precedence versus Bank standard terms; and Secured Party third-party beneficiary / agent-assignment mechanics (collectively MEDIUM to HIGH depending on operational facts).

The companion deliverable aca-redline.docx implements tracked deletions and insertions curing each issue. This memorandum identifies every deviation and gap with section references, playbook requirements, risk ratings, exposure analysis, recommended positions, and a summary deviation matrix.

Recommendation: Do not execute the counterparty draft as presented. Circulate aca-redline.docx; treat Issues 1–3 as walk-away / partner-level points; treat missing-protection inserts as standard required fixes before CP satisfaction under the Credit Agreement collateral package.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
II. SCOPE, MATERIALS, AND METHODOLOGY
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

A. Materials Reviewed
  • Counterparty markup / draft ACA (Matter Doc: “Counterparty markup — contracts work: Review Account Control Agreement Counterparty Paper”).
  • Base deal materials and engagement instruction (Matter Doc: “Deal materials — contracts work: Review Account Control Agreement Counterparty Paper”).
  • Internal ACA / deposit-account control playbook standards (firm precedent: secured-party favorable control, NOEC mechanics, indemnity carve-outs for failure to honor entitlement orders, tiered survival, NY/UCC alignment).
  • Executed Credit Agreement framework: collateral perfection by control; blocked/springing account mechanics; Event of Default → enforcement; agent succession; Loan Document supremacy as between Debtor and Secured Party.
  • Depository bank standard form expectations: ministerial role, ordinary-negligence cap market, but not silent reduction below playbook floors; not tipping baskets on bank ops liability for control failures; not 5-Business-Day “commercially reasonable efforts” exclusive-control timing.
  • Account details / checklists: Schedule A accuracy, authorized signers, fee schedule, correspondence on account setup.

B. Methodology
  • Line-compare counterparty operative terms to playbook requirements and Credit Agreement collateral covenants.
  • Flag silent changes (especially economic risk allocations) as elevated risk.
  • Rate each issue: HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW by enforcement impact, perfection/priority impact, and dollars-at-risk.
  • Prescribe Accept / Reject / Counter with fallback, mapped to redline sections in aca-redline.docx.
  • Build summary deviation matrix (Section VIII).

C. Counterparty-Identified Deviations (from markup cover note)
  The counterparty’s own revision note concedes three intentional shifts:
  (1) indemnification cap silently reduced; basket converted from deductible to tipping basket;
  (2) MAE definition adds carve-outs for regulatory action of the kind at issue;
  (3) new limitation period shortens survival for core representations.
  Each is addressed in full below, together with additional gaps not flagged by counterparty.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
III. ISSUE-BY-ISSUE ANALYSIS
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

════════════════════════════════════
ISSUE 1 — Indemnification Cap Reduction and Basket Conversion
════════════════════════════════════

Section references (counterparty draft / redline):
  • Definitions: “Indemnification Cap”; “Basket”
  • Article VI (Indemnification; Limitation of Liability), especially § 6.2
  • Related: damage-waiver breadth; interaction with account agreement fee schedules

Playbook / Credit Agreement / market requirement:
  • Playbook: Bank ordinary-negligence liability may be capped at the greater of (x) 36 months of fees under the ACA and (y) a fixed floor (playbook standard $5,000,000), BUT caps and baskets must NEVER apply to: gross negligence, willful misconduct, bad faith, fraud, failure to comply with NOEC/entitlement orders, or breach of exclusive-control obligations (“Excluded Matters”).
  • Basket must be a true deductible (excess-only), not a tipping basket; playbook floor $500,000 for ordinary-negligence claims; Basket inapplicable to Excluded Matters and Fundamental Representations.
  • Silent reduction of caps or conversion of basket type is a non-starter; any side letter or fee schedule attempting the same is void as against Secured Party unless signed by Secured Party.
  • Credit Agreement: Agent and Lenders require full recourse for bank operational failure that impairs Control or Collateral proceeds; limitations that effectively eliminate recovery for failure to honor a NOEC are inconsistent with perfection and enforcement architecture.

Counterparty position:
  • Cap reduced to twelve (12) months of Bank fees (no fixed-dollar floor).
  • Basket set at $250,000 and converted to a tipping basket (once exceeded, recovery from dollar one — but more importantly, paired with a low cap this is used to re-characterize risk; the adverse element versus playbook is the conversion away from deductible PLUS the lowered threshold and the application of cap/basket even to control failures).
  • Broad consequential-damages waiver and cap purport to cover negligence and operational errors including entitlement-order failures.

Risk rating: HIGH

Exposure analysis:
  • Economic: On a low-fee operational ACA, 12 months of fees can be a de minimis five- or six-figure number — orders of magnitude below expected loss if Bank fails to freeze or misdirects a concentration-account balance post-default (often eight figures in middle-market / upper-middle-market facilities).
  • Perfection / enforcement: If Bank honors Debtor wires after NOEC or delays exclusive control, Secured Party’s practical recovery may be the only meaningful remedy; a tiny cap converts a control agreement into a paper perfection device without teeth.
  • Litigation: Tipping basket + low cap + broad consequential waiver creates briefing risk that even direct losses are squeezed; silent change increases “we thought you accepted” estoppel arguments if not redlined out.
  • Regulatory overlay: Where regulatory action against Debtor or Bank is a live risk (see Issue 2), operational errors around freezes and levies become more likely — exactly when uncapped Excluded Matter liability is needed.

Recommended position:
  • REJECT counterparty cap and tipping basket.
  • COUNTER (primary — as in aca-redline.docx):
      – Indemnification Cap = greater of (x) 36 months’ fees and (y) $5,000,000, applicable solely to ordinary negligence in ministerial duties.
      – Basket = $500,000 true deductible; excess-only; does not apply to Excluded Matters, Fundamental Representations, or fraud.
      – Express Excluded Matters carve-out from cap, basket, and consequential-damages waiver, including failure to comply with NOEC/entitlement orders and exclusive-control breaches.
      – Anti-silent-amendment clause: fee schedules / account agreements cannot reduce these protections without Secured Party signature.
  • Fallback (partner approval): Cap at greater of 24 months’ fees or $2,500,000; deductible Basket $250,000; but Excluded Matters remain fully uncapped — no fallback on Excluded Matters carve-out.
  • Walk-away: Any construct that caps or baskets liability for failure to honor NOEC or entitlement orders.

Redline implementation: aca-redline.docx Definitions (Indemnification Cap, Basket, Excluded Matter, Losses, Indemnified Person); Article VI §§ 6.1–6.3; Endnote RN-1.

════════════════════════════════════
ISSUE 2 — Material Adverse Effect: Regulatory-Action Carve-Outs
════════════════════════════════════

Section references:
  • Article I — Definition of “Material Adverse Effect”
  • Cross-references: bring-down conditions (if any in ACA), termination rights, Debtor covenants tied to MAE, interaction with Credit Agreement MAE/Event of Default

Playbook / Credit Agreement / market requirement:
  • Playbook: ACA MAE (if used) must protect (a) business/financial condition, (b) ability to perform, (c) enforceability of ACA and Liens, and (d) Secured Party rights/remedies and Lien validity/perfection/priority. Carve-outs, if any, apply only to clause (a), must include a “disproportionate effect” backstop, and must NOT carve out regulatory actions, investigations, enforcement proceedings, consent orders, fines, sanctions, or supervisory directives.
  • Credit Agreement: Regulatory events are often independently material to Defaults, cash dominion, and collateral value. An ACA that defines away regulatory MAE creates inconsistency and borrower arguments that account-control enforcement or related drawstops are unavailable.
  • Matter-specific: Counterparty expressly added carve-outs “for regulatory action of exactly the kind at issue in this matter.” That is a targeted risk shift and is unacceptable.

Counterparty position:
  • MAE limited essentially to traditional business MAE.
  • Broad proviso carving out, among other things, “any regulatory action, investigation, enforcement proceeding, consent order, fine, sanction, or supervisory directive by any Governmental Authority (including bank regulatory, consumer financial, anti-money-laundering, sanctions, or prudential regulators) affecting the Debtor, the Deposit Account, the Bank, or the transactions contemplated hereby.”
  • No disproportionate-impact limiter; carve-outs bleed into enforceability concepts by structure of the definition.

Risk rating: HIGH

Exposure analysis:
  • Directly disables contractual triggers if the very regulatory scenario the deal team is underwriting materializes.
  • Creates conflict with Credit Agreement MAE/Default structure — borrower will cite ACA definition in inter-document disputes.
  • Impairs negotiation leverage for NOEC delivery, supplemental collateral demands, and lender-liability optics if Bank or Debtor is under consent order.
  • Off-market for secured-party ACA paper; regulatory carve-outs of this breadth are buy-side / borrower wish-list items, not bank-form standard in agent-drafted control agreements.

Recommended position:
  • REJECT regulatory-action carve-out in its entirety.
  • COUNTER (primary — as in redline):
      – Four-prong MAE: (a) business/financial; (b) performance ability; (c) legality/enforceability of Agreement and Liens; (d) Secured Party rights/remedies and Lien perfection/priority.
      – Carve-outs only to clause (a); standard market list (general economic/political, GAAP/law of general applicability, war/terrorism/natural disasters, announcement of the deal); each subject to disproportionate-adverse-effect backstop.
      – Express “for the avoidance of doubt” that regulatory actions are NOT carved out and may constitute MAE under any prong.
  • Fallback: Limited carve-out for industry-wide regulatory changes of general application (not entity-specific enforcement), still subject to disproportionate-effect qualifier; entity-specific investigations, consent orders, fines remain inside MAE. No fallback that carves out entity-specific regulatory action “of the kind at issue.”
  • Walk-away: Retention of the counterparty’s regulatory carve-out language.

Redline implementation: aca-redline.docx § 1.1 Material Adverse Effect; Endnote RN-2.

════════════════════════════════════
ISSUE 3 — Shortened Survival / Limitation Period for Core Representations
════════════════════════════════════

Section references:
  • Article I — “Survival Period”; “Fundamental Representations” (insert)
  • Article IV — Representations; survival clause (§ 4.7 in redline)
  • Article VII — Termination; survival of indemnities and reps (§ 7.3)

Playbook / Credit Agreement / market requirement:
  • Playbook tiered survival:
      – Fundamental Representations (org, authority, enforceability, no conflict, deposit account title/control, no prior control agreements/priority, sanctions/AML as applicable): through applicable statute of limitations + 90 days (or equivalent), and Control/authority concepts effectively evergreen or ≥ 6 years if Bank demands a number.
      – Other reps: 36 months after earlier of termination and Discharge Date.
      – Claims asserted in writing before expiry continue until final resolution.
      – Fraud / willful misconduct: not shortened by contract.
  • Credit Agreement: Perfection, priority, and enforceability issues often surface at enforcement — years after signing. A 12-month cliff extinguishing core reps (and “including then-pending claims”) is incompatible with collateral reliability.
  • Market: Borrower-style long-stop survival on M&A reps is not analogous; ACA fundamental reps are closer to continuous collateral warranties.

Counterparty position:
  • Single Survival Period: twelve (12) months following termination of the Agreement.
  • Purports to terminate reps in full after that period, including as to then-pending claims.
  • No Fundamental Representations tier; no statute-of-limitations tether; no fraud carve-out stated.

Risk rating: HIGH

Exposure analysis:
  • If a competing control agreement, undisclosed adverse claim, or authority defect appears after month 12, Secured Party may face “rep expired” defenses precisely when enforcement value is needed.
  • Extinguishing pending claims is particularly off-market and aggressive — creates artificial claim-acceleration and waiver risk.
  • Interacts badly with Issue 1: short survival + low cap + tipping basket = stacked limitation architecture.
  • Bank may legitimately want temporal limits on soft reps; playbook already accommodates that via tiering — counterparty over-reached by collapsing all tiers to 12 months.

Recommended position:
  • REJECT 12-month unitary survival and any extinguishment of timely-asserted claims.
  • COUNTER (primary — as in redline):
      – Define Fundamental Representations (org; authorization/enforceability; no conflict; deposit account/title/control; no prior control agreements/priority; compliance/sanctions/AML).
      – Survival Period: (a) Fundamental Reps → SOL + 90 days; (b) Control/authority/enforceability/bank-regulatory-capacity → unlimited or minimum 6 years post-termination; (c) other reps → 36 months post earlier of termination and Discharge Date.
      – Written claims before expiry survive until resolution.
      – Fraud/willful misconduct unaffected; no contractual shortening of SOL for fraud or for enforcement of Control/priority.
  • Fallback: Fundamental Reps 6 years from execution; other reps 24 months post-termination; pending claims preserved; fraud evergreen. Do not accept < 24 months on Fundamental Reps or any “pending claims die” formulation.
  • Walk-away: 12-month cliff on core/control reps; extinguishment of pending claims.

Redline implementation: aca-redline.docx Definitions (Survival Period, Fundamental Representations, Discharge Date); § 4.7; § 7.3; Endnote RN-3.

════════════════════════════════════
ISSUE 4 — Weak / Missing UCC Control and Exclusive-Control Timing
════════════════════════════════════

Section references:
  • Article III (§§ 3.1–3.5 in redline)
  • Counterparty draft: “commercially reasonable efforts” to comply with NOEC within five (5) Business Days

Playbook requirement:
  • Express agreement that Bank will comply with Secured Party instructions without further Debtor consent (UCC § 9-104(a)(2)).
  • Same-day / next-Business-Day hard timing for NOEC and entitlement orders (if received before noon local, same day; else next Business Day).
  • Immediate cessation of Debtor instructions at Effectiveness Time; written confirmation of NOEC receipt and balance within one Business Day.
  • No dual-control or Debtor countersignature condition after NOEC; sweep/ZBA auto-terminates at NOEC unless Secured Party directs otherwise.

Risk rating: HIGH (perfection practical enforcement) / MEDIUM-HIGH (timing alone)

Exposure analysis:
  • Five Business Days of “efforts” post-default is an open window for Debtor drains; defeats cash dominion.
  • Ambiguous control language invites UCC priority disputes with subsequent secured parties or levy creditors.
  • Credit Agreement blocked-account covenants assume instantaneous or near-instantaneous dominion upon election.

Recommended position:
  • REJECT 5-Business-Day commercially reasonable efforts standard.
  • INSERT full Article III mechanics per aca-redline.docx (control statement; Effectiveness Time consequences; hard timing; reliance; no dual control; sweep/ZBA).
  • Fallback on timing only: next Business Day absolute outside noon rule; never more than two Business Days. No fallback on “without further Debtor consent” control language.

Redline: Article III; Endnote RN-4.

════════════════════════════════════
ISSUE 5 — Bank Lien Subordination and Post-NOEC Set-Off
════════════════════════════════════

Section references:
  • § 2.2 (redline); Bank standard form set-off clauses often left intact by counterparty draft

Playbook requirement:
  • Bank subordinates security interests, set-off, banker’s lien, and counterclaims to Secured Party, with narrow ordinary-course fee and returned-item exceptions.
  • After Effectiveness Time, no set-off/recoupment/banker’s lien without Secured Party consent (other than pre-NOEC returned items).

Risk rating: HIGH

Exposure analysis:
  • Unsubordinated set-off allows Bank to deplete Account Collateral at enforcement — classic priority leak.
  • Off-market for agent-drafted ACAs; Bank forms that preserve broad set-off must be overridden.

Recommended position:
  • INSERT § 2.2 subordination and post-NOEC freeze as redlined.
  • Fallback: Permit set-off for Bank’s ACA fees only, capped monthly, still prohibited if Bank is in breach of exclusive-control duties.

Redline: § 2.2; RN-4.

════════════════════════════════════
ISSUE 6 — No-Other-Control-Agreement; Priority Representations
════════════════════════════════════

Section references:
  • §§ 2.3, 4.5 (redline inserts)
